unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: More specifically, the inner product $Z^\top a$ between the generic random vector $Z\in\mathbb R^d$, with components $Z_s$ for $s=1,\ldots,d$, and the vector of coefficients $a\in\mathbb R^d$ having elements $a_s$ for $s=1,\ldots,d$, is expressed as $a_sZ_s$, with the sum being implicit in the repetition of the indexes. Similarly, if $B$ is a $d\times d$ matrix with entries $b_{st}$ for $s,t=1,\ldots,d$, the quadratic form $Z^\top BZ$ is expressed as $b_{st}Z_sZ_t$. The generalization to operations involving arrays with higher dimensions is obtained under the same reasoning.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original Einstein-index convention; repeated indexes are summed, not free parameters. Marginal formulas later restrict the respective index sets.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: The Euclidean norm of a vector $a\in\mathbb R^d$ is denoted by $\|a\|$, whereas, for a generic $d\times d$ matrix $B$, the notation $|B|$ indicates its determinant, while $\lambda_{\mathrm{MIN}}(B)$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{MAX}}(B)$ its minimum and maximum eigenvalue, respectively. Furthermore, $u\wedge v$ and $u\vee v$ correspond to $\min\{u,v\}$ and $\max\{u,v\}$. For two positive sequences $u_n,v_n$ we employ $u_n\lesssim v_n$ if there exists a universal positive constant $C$ such that $u_n\le Cv_n$. When $u_n\lesssim v_n$ and $v_n\lesssim u_n$ are satisfied simultaneously, we write $u_n\asymp v_n$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Ambient norm, determinant, eigenvalue and comparison notation. Assumption10 separately calls its matrix/tensor norm spectral.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
\[
\ell_{\widehat\theta,stl}^{(3)}\widehat h_s\widehat h_t\widehat h_l+3\ell_{\widehat\theta,str}^{(3)}\widehat h_s\widehat h_t\mathbb E_{\widehat h_{\bar C}\mid\widehat h_C}(\widehat h_r)+3\ell_{\widehat\theta,srv}^{(3)}\widehat h_s\mathbb E_{\widehat h_{\bar C}\mid\widehat h_C}(\widehat h_r\widehat h_v)+\ell_{\widehat\theta,rvk}^{(3)}\mathbb E_{\widehat h_{\bar C}\mid\widehat h_C}(\widehat h_r\widehat h_v\widehat h_k),\tag{28}
\]
with $s,t,l\in C$ and $r,v,k\in\bar C$. Therefore, the above expected values simply require the first three non–central moments of the multivariate Gaussian having density $\phi_{d-d_C}(\widehat h_{\bar C};\Lambda_C\widehat h_C,\bar\Omega)$. These are $\mathbb E_{\widehat h_{\bar C}\mid\widehat h_C}(\widehat h_r)=\Lambda_{C,rl}\widehat h_l$, $\mathbb E_{\widehat h_{\bar C}\mid\widehat h_C}(\widehat h_r\widehat h_v)=\bar\Omega_{rv}+\Lambda_{C,rt}\Lambda_{C,vl}\widehat h_t\widehat h_l$ and $\mathbb E_{\widehat h_{\bar C}\mid\widehat h_C}(\widehat h_r\widehat h_v\widehat h_k)=3\bar\Omega_{rv}\Lambda_{C,ks}\widehat h_s+\Lambda_{C,rs}\Lambda_{C,vt}\Lambda_{C,kl}\widehat h_s\widehat h_t\widehat h_l$.

Under Assumptions 5–8, there exists a sufficiently–large $c_0>0$ in $M_n=\sqrt{c_0\log n}$, such that for every $D>0$ it holds

source_issues.note: Registered arXiv2301.03038v3 marked8Apr2024,54pages. Main text ends on29 before REFERENCES y248.679; evidence clipped242. Supplementary bodies starting32 are excluded. Exactly three main-text Theorems are retained.

The common dominating measure covers both true and model distributions; non-i.i.d. and misspecified models are allowed. The KL projection is indexed through P_theta^n but theta_* is not given an n index. Preserve the source notation and its unique-projection Assumption1; do not assume iid samples or substitute a correctly specified true parameter.

Assumption2 defines K_n using theta distance <=M_n delta_n, but immediately takes a supremum over h in K_n. The proof later uses h-space balls. Preserve original definition and record coordinate mismatch, rather than silently replacing K_n in the assumption.

Assumption3 literally prints log pi(theta_*+delta_n h)/pi(theta_*) without parentheses around the ratio, unlike the explicit ratio in the earlier univariate expansion. Archive exactly and note intended log-ratio scope is ambiguous under literal operator precedence.

F is allowed with eta in R, but the skew polynomial divides by eta. A CDF derivative is nonnegative and eta=0 is possible under the stated conditions. Do not insert eta>0 into original text. The approximating covariance is guaranteed only on a high-probability event; no fallback on its complement is supplied in the theorem. Assumption2 does not explicitly state symmetry of V or the third-order array.

The text says w lies in (0,1), although a general allowed CDF can reach0 or1. It uses cdf notation P(S)=integral_S p for generic sets, and overloads Pi_n/pi_n under rescaling. Preserve text and identify measures/densities in analysis without changing quotations.

MAP is a global argmax; the source states its score plus prior score is zero by definition. That requires an interior differentiable maximizer, which is not automatic on constrained Theta. Theorem4.1 does not explicitly repeat Theorem2.1 interior-point hypothesis. Record the issue; do not add a new hypothesis or replace the MAP with the MLE.

Skew-modal covariance uses J_hat_theta from negative log-likelihood Hessian divided by n, not the negative full log-posterior Hessian. Prior second derivatives appear in Assumption10 bounds. Preserve their separate roles and probability events.
